tier_reason: benchmarks/polyglot/RESULTS.md runs the same TypeScript sources (benchmarks/suite/*.ts, with bench.cpp/.rs/.java peers and run_all.sh public) under Perry v0.5.908 default mode and Node v25.8.0 / Bun 1.3.12, with compiler versions and release-mode-only flags in METHODOLOGY.md and the CPU named (Apple M1 Max), median of 11 runs; first-party but fully reproducible, so A stands.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Polyglot RESULTS.md (Perry v0.5.908 default mode, Apple M1 Max, median of 11 runs): fibonacci Perry 309 ms vs Node 987 ms (3.2x, derived from page data) vs Bun 518 ms vs Java 278 ms; array_write 3 vs 9 ms; object_create 2 vs 8 ms; accumulate 97 vs 597 ms (6.2x, derived from page data; the page attributes Node's gap to V8 not inlining fmod); array_read 11 vs 14 ms. Perry loses loop_overhead (97 ms vs Node 53, Bun 41) and ties loop_data_dependent (225 vs 226), math_intensive (51 vs 49) and nested_loops (18 vs 17). The newer auto-generated RESULTS_AUTO.md (2026-09-01, Perry v0.5.1519, x86_64 Linux, taskset-pinned) has fibonacci 323 vs Node 708 ms and accumulate 58 vs 162 ms, but Perry slower than Node on nested_loops (26 vs 15) and math_intensive (51 vs 44). honest_bench REPORT.md at the README's pinned revision 7beb3a50ca (v0.5.908, M1 Max): image convolution Perry 354.0 ms vs Node 1,206.6 ms (3.4x) vs Bun 915.4 vs Rust 392.1; JSON pipeline 100 records 39.2 vs Node 143.6 ms; JSON 500k records Perry 1,098.4 vs Node 966.3 vs Bun 649.9 ms (Perry slower). The same file at HEAD (generated 2026-09-01, perry 0.5.1519, unnamed x86_64 host): convolution Perry 1,204.4 ms vs Node 975.0 ms (Perry 1.24x slower, derived from page data); JSON 100 records 19.6 vs 53.0 ms; JSON 500k 1,831.2 vs 1,183.5 ms. The '268 ms, 4.5x faster than Node' bottom line is stale prose hard-coded in honest_bench/scripts/report.py, not a current measurement. README's public Node/Bun suite (results/public-node-bun-v1.json): Perry loses method_calls (35 vs Node 11 ms), binary_trees (13 vs 6) and prime_sieve (6 vs 5), wins matrix_multiply (19 vs 33) and json_roundtrip (144 vs 379).
corrections.hardware: Apple M1 Max (10 cores, 64 GB RAM), macOS 26.4 for polyglot RESULTS.md and for honest_bench at pinned revision 7beb3a50ca; honest_bench REPORT.md at HEAD and polyglot RESULTS_AUTO.md (both 2026-09-01, v0.5.1519) ran on an x86_64 16-core Ubuntu 24.04 / Linux 6.17 host whose CPU model is not stated
corrections.caveats: AOT compiler measured against V8's JIT, included because the claim is against Node/V8. Results are mixed and the repo says so: HotSpot Java beats Perry on fibonacci, Node wins loop_overhead, and the README's public Node/Bun suite shows Perry losing method_calls (3x), binary_trees and prime_sieve. Several polyglot wins are 2-9 ms cells where noise matters, and accumulate's 6x comes from V8 not inlining fmod. METHODOLOGY.md lists Perry v0.5.585 while RESULTS.md reports v0.5.908, and RESULTS.md's prose cites stale numbers (array_read 3 ms, Node 322 ms on loop_data_dependent) that disagree with its own table (11 ms, 226 ms). honest_bench REPORT.md is internally inconsistent at HEAD: scripts/report.py hard-codes v0.5.81-era bottom-line prose (Perry 268 ms on convolution, 4.5x faster than Node; JSON 500k 1,649 ms) above freshly generated tables in which Perry is slower than Node on convolution (1,204.4 vs 975.0 ms, sigma 282) and on JSON 500k (1,831.2 vs 1,183.5 ms). The README pins its convolution and JSON-100 figures to revision 7beb3a50ca (M1 Max, v0.5.908: 354.0 vs 1,206.6 ms), but its 500k-record JSON row (1,649 / 1,010 / 647 / 604 ms) matches the stale hard-coded prose, not that revision's table (1,098.4 / 966.3 / 649.9 / 608.3 ms); its note that HEAD reads 0.0 ms is also out of date (regenerated with real numbers in #9405, 2026-09-01). The newest x86_64 sweeps do not name the CPU model. Written by the project itself with a 'we publish everything' framing; the README highlight table selects favourable rows.

notes: Polyglot RESULTS.md numbers match the record and the page meets tier A. The search agent's inconsistency flag is correct and has a cause: honest_bench/scripts/report.py hard-codes stale v0.5.81 bottom-line prose (268 ms, 4.5x vs Node) above regenerated tables in which Perry is now slower than Node on convolution (1,204.4 vs 975.0 ms on x86_64, v0.5.1519); the README's 500k JSON row also comes from that stale prose rather than its pinned 7beb3a50ca revision. Record shortcomings: mixed results versus Node, stale or contradictory prose in the project's reports, unnamed CPU on the newest x86_64 runs.

tier_reason: Independent third-party JMH suite (ionutbalosin/jvm-performance-benchmarks, JDK 25 results committed 2026-04-13) with public code, JMH options and JVM args in settings/benchmarks-suite-jdk25.json, and per-benchmark CSVs; compiler.csv shows C2 1.00 vs GraalVM CE 0.84 over 298 benchmarks. No CPU model or exact JDK build is stated anywhere opened, so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: JDK 25 (exact OpenJDK, GraalVM CE and Oracle GraalVM builds not stated); JMH options -wi 5 -w 10 -i 5 -r 10 -f 5 and JVM args -Xms4g -Xmx4g -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch for every benchmark (settings/benchmarks-suite-jdk25.json); GraalVM CE and Oracle GraalVM JIT vs OpenJDK HotSpot C2
corrections.caveats: The numbers are in a third-party suite, not in the oracle/graal repo, whose README gives no performance figures. No CPU model or exact JDK build is stated in the suite README, settings, PR #115 or result CSVs (README covers OS tuning only), which is why this is tier B rather than A. The compiler category is made of handwritten patterns chosen to exercise optimizations, so the 16% geomean gap is not an application speedup; the other categories are smaller (api 0.92 over 756 benchmarks, miscellaneous 0.91 over 82, whole suite 0.9 over 1136, in sibling geomean CSVs). Normalized geometric means hide per-benchmark losses. GraalVM CE and Oracle GraalVM results are within run-to-run noise of each other (e.g. FibonacciBenchmark CSVs), so the Oracle build shows no extra gain here. The suite itself is Apache-2.0; graal's compiler is GPL-2.0 with Classpath Exception while other graal components carry UPL, BSD-3-Clause and GPL-2.0. The suite author's articles for JDK 17 and 21 (blog host) were not opened.

notes: compiler.csv and summary.csv match the record exactly (C2 1.00 vs Graal CE/Oracle 0.84 over 298; HotSpot 1.0 vs 0.9 over 1136). JVM flags are public, CPU model is not; keep at B. Shortcomings: microbenchmark-pattern geomean, no CPU model, CE and Oracle GraalVM indistinguishable.

tier_reason: First-party README table of pure CPython 3.8/3.9 vs DIO-JIT with public timeit scripts in benchmarks/, but no hardware, units, CPython build or run count; C.

corrections.workload: Seven small Python programs (brainfuck interpreter, append3, DNA read, fib(15), hypot on strings, selection sort, trans), pure CPython versus the same code under the DIO-JIT decorator; each script in benchmarks/ times a fixed number of calls with timeit (fib.py 100,000 calls of f(15), trans.py 111,111,111 calls), so the README figures are presumably total seconds, though the table states no units.
corrections.caveats: No hardware, no units, no CPython build details, and no comparison with PyPy, which is the strong baseline for Python JIT speed. Only microbenchmarks. The docstring timings inside the scripts (fib 1.33 s vs 0.18 s, trans 2.68 s vs 0.85 s) differ from the README table, so the table came from a separate unrecorded run. In fib.py the pure-Python baseline uses a - 1 while the JIT version uses a + -1 because no rule for subtraction exists. The README's 500x partial-evaluation example (benchmarks/const_fib.py) specialises the function on the literal value 20 (jit.ofval(20)), so the JIT side returns a constant-folded result; it is not a general speedup. Requires Julia plus the DIO.jl package at runtime; no for loops, exception handling or closures inside JIT functions; README says not production-ready. LICENSE is BSD-2-Clause but setup.py declares 'mit'. Last commit 2021-02-18.

notes: README numbers match the record. Tier C stands. Shortcomings: no PyPy comparison, no hardware or units, 500x claim is constant folding on a literal argument, Julia runtime dependency, abandoned since 2021-02-18, license metadata mismatch (LICENSE BSD-2-Clause vs setup.py 'mit').
